parsed.explanation: Combined regime: this state imposes no adult bathroom or adult-care ban and four municipalities cover 46% of residents, but national visa screening treats document/sex discrepancy as grounds for refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal policy bars identity-congruent government facilities, and immigration custody has documented forced labour and sexual abuse. Courts and litigation provide real but incomplete recourse; statewide discrimination/hate-crime gaps remain. Youth measures are board/draft and district-level, not an operative adult ban.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable: discrepancy or doubt about applicant sex requires refusal and added evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility. X/mismatched markers no longer issued nationally; passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud requires four elements, limited waivers possible, never automatic; civil-liberties suit pending and courts have enjoined some orders.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport mismatch at visa stage can move visitor from entry screening to investigation, refusal, and potential detention, despite state-level absence of adult bans.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports: transgender men subjected to forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National corrections model from 2026 reportedly cuts hair, removes hormones, substitutes psychiatric treatment/drugs.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor-specific custody protocol; national hate-crime statute exists but state hate-crime law omits gender identity, limiting enhancement/recourse for bias violence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention is not the routine consequence of presence, but if visa/facility/trespass encounter escalates, custody placement and abuse risk become the severe end of the chain.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State itself has no statewide adult restroom ban; one school district requires birth-sex or private nurse-office use for students.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No statewide adult facility prohibition; four municipalities prohibit gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations, covering about 46% of population; one ordinance survived repeal vote 53-47.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings/funded facilities can impose the national restriction even inside a state without an adult ban; outside those settings state adult access is not banned.

care_services.exposure: Adult gender-affirming care is not banned statewide. National proposed October 2025 rule would bar public insurance for under-18 care; several national orders have been blocked/enjoined, status unresolved per measure.
care_services.protection: No statewide adult care ban documented. State medical board youth action is recommendation plus draft only, pending law-department vetting and 30-day comment, not operative.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor care continuity is not documented as refused by state law; minor care exposure is regulatory/draft and national-proposed rather than enacted statewide.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: January 2025 order redefines sex as binary at birth, rescinds pronoun/name policies, bans trans athletes entering for women's sports. May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; December 2025 memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' as extremist viewpoint, not reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling and national hate-crimes statute remain; challenges to executive orders and passport policy pending; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises screening and investigation discretion, but dossier does not document visitor arrests for identity itself in this state; functioning courts have sometimes blocked measures.

minors_guardians.exposure: Education board barred transgender students from female sports statewide (2023); one district imposes birth-sex/private bathrooms; medical board draft would make under-18 transition care unprofessional conduct for clinicians.
minors_guardians.protection: Draft youth regulation not operative; governor's earlier statewide student facility limit failed; no documented parental criminalisation for travelling with a minor, and no adult care ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling minor is mainly exposed if seeking school enrolment, sports, or youth care, not through an adult visitor ban; parent/guardian risk is indirect via provider discipline and school policy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No count of trans-specific violence or general homicide rate in state inventory, so pattern cannot be assessed. State lacks gender-identity hate-crime enhancement; 2025 poll found 66% support birth-sex on documents, indicating hostile policy attitudes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute punishes gender-identity hate crimes; municipal ordinances in four municipalities provide local discrimination recourse, though enforcement reach is not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outside those municipalities, visitor has no state/municipal discrimination recourse in hotels, restaurants or workplaces, so street/service hostility may go unremedied locally.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are fragmented: passport suit unresolved, several orders enjoined but others in effect, enforcement of four municipal ordinances not documented, bias-crime police guidance not in inventory.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have allowed suits, enjoined some orders, and voters rejected a bathroom restriction; legal-aid FAQ guidance exists for document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists but is slow, uneven by municipality and federal/state stage, and does not nullify operative visa/federal-facility restrictions while litigation proceeds.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-B because no routine police stops, confiscation, fines or district exclusion for transgender visitors is documented in this state, and courts have enjoined measures; higher severity appears only via visa-fraud and custody chains, not routine detention.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow remedies dominate, with administrative denial and humiliation more typical than imprisonment. Added federal facility exclusion and documented custody abuse pull the case toward the lower end of this tier.

Lower than 0.65-A and 0.65-B because there is no documented prompt apology, compensation, or ombudsperson reversal for this visitor class; instead national policy creates refusal/fraud risk and statewide discrimination/hate-crime recourse is absent outside four municipalities.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction: state adult law is comparatively permissive, but national entry, federal-facility, and custody regimes follow the visitor into every stage. A document discrepancy can trigger refusal and fraud investigation; detention, if it follows, carries documented severe abuse. Municipal protections cover less than half the population with unproven enforcement, while courts provide partial, pending relief. For minors, operative exposure is limited to sports and one district's school policy, as youth-care restriction remains a draft. Net: elevated-to-reduced risk, centred near 0.55.
